category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Define Biosafety and Biosafety Levels (BSL) according to WHO guidelines.
back:
1. Biosafety: Principles and practices preventing unintentional exposure or accidental release of biological agents.
2. BSL (1-4): Facility designations based on design, equipment, and procedures required to handle specific risk groups.
citation: Source: Patient safety ID.md: [Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release. Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures required to work with agents from various risk groups.]

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: How does the WHO define Biosafety in laboratory settings?
back: The containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents/toxins or their accidental release.
citation: Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What are the two primary airflow engineering controls required for a BSL-3 facility?
back:
1. Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into the lab).
2. HEPA filtration of all exhaust air.
citation: BSL-3... Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Contrast BSL-1 and BSL-2 regarding access and benchwork procedures.
back:
BSL-1: Open benchwork permitted; standard access.
BSL-2: Restricted lab access; Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) required for aerosol-generating procedures.
citation: BSL-1: open benchwork... BSL-2: Restricted lab access... Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: A lab handles Ebola virus. Identify the BSL level and the required personal suit type.
back:
Level: BSL-4.
Suit: Positive-pressure air-fed suits (or Class III glove-box BSC).
citation: BSL-4... Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus... Safety Protocols: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: List the four factors the WHO uses to designate a Biosafety Level (BSL).
back:
1. Lab design and construction.
2. Containment facilities.
3. Equipment.
4. Operational procedures/practices.
citation: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned... based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Which specific risk group and organism example characterize BSL-1?
back:
Risk Group: RG-1 (agents not known to cause disease in healthy adults).
Example: E. coli (K-12 strains).
citation: BSL-1... RG-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans... E. coli (K-12 strains).

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Why is a double-door entry airlock mandatory for BSL-3 laboratories?
back: To maintain controlled negative air pressure and prevent the release of infectious aerosols during entry/exit.
citation: BSL-3... Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab)... double-door entry airlock.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Differentiate BSL-3 and BSL-4 based on risk and available treatment.
back:
BSL-3: Serious/lethal inhalation risk; treatments usually exist.
BSL-4: Life-threatening risk; no vaccines or treatments available; high community risk.
citation: BSL-3: agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation... BSL-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk... with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What is the mandatory exit procedure for personnel in a BSL-4 facility?
back: A full chemical decontamination shower exit is required.
citation: BSL-4... Safety Protocols: full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Name three moderate-hazard pathogens requiring BSL-2 containment.
back:
1. Hepatitis B & C viruses.
2. HIV.
3. Salmonella spp.
citation: BSL-2... Bio-Risk Organisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: How does the WHO define Biosafety in a laboratory or clinical context?
back: Containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents/toxins or their accidental release.
citation: Section 1: Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What defines Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) according to WHO?
back: Designations assigned to lab facilities based on design, construction, equipment, and practices required to handle specific risk group agents safely.
citation: Section 1: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Differentiate between the organisms handled in BSL-1 versus BSL-2 laboratories.
back: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents (e.g., E. coli K-12) not known to cause disease. BSL-2: Moderate hazard agents (e.g., HBV, HIV, Salmonella).
citation: Section 1: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease... BSL-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel (Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., HBV, HIV).

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: A lab processes Mycobacterium tuberculosis samples. Which BSL and specific airflow system are mandatory?
back: BSL-3. Requires controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into the lab) and HEPA filtration of exhaust air.
citation: Section 1: BSL-3: Indigenous or exotic agents (Mycobacterium tuberculosis)... Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Which laboratory equipment is essential for aerosol-generating procedures in BSL-2?
back: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) must be used for centrifugation, vortexing, or other aerosol-generating steps.
citation: Section 1: BSL-2 Safety Protocols: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What are the core characteristics of Risk Group 4 (RG-4) pathogens?
back: Dangerous, exotic agents; high individual/community risk; life-threatening aerosol-transmitted infections; no available vaccines or treatments (e.g., Ebola).
citation: Section 1: RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Identify three facility design features unique to BSL-3 compared to BSL-2.
back: 1. Double-door entry airlock. 2. Hands-free sinks. 3. Directional negative airflow (controlled air pressure).
citation: Section 1: BSL-3 Facility Features: Controlled negative air pressure; double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: An outbreak of Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever occurs. Which lab facility and PPE are required?
back: BSL-4. Requires an isolated building, positive-pressure air-fed suits, and double-HEPA filtered exhaust.
citation: Section 1: BSL-4: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus... Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits; double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Explain the primary route of transmission for agents handled in BSL-3 facilities.
back: Transmission occurs primarily through the inhalation or aerosol route, causing serious or potentially lethal disease.
citation: Section 1: BSL-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What is the standard waste disposal requirement for BSL-2 facilities?
back: Autoclave must be available for decontaminating biological waste before disposal or recycling.
citation: Section 1: BSL-2: Autoclave available for waste... Treated by Autoclaving or Microwaving followed by shredding.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Define Biosafety according to WHO.
back: The containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents/toxins or their accidental release.
citation: Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Explain the directional airflow requirement in a BSL-3 laboratory.
back: Controlled negative air pressure ensures air flows into the lab, preventing aerosol escape; exhaust air must be HEPA-filtered.
citation: BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Contrast BSL-2 and BSL-3 based on primary transmission routes.
back:
BSL-2: Ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane exposure.
BSL-3: Serious or lethal disease via inhalation/aerosol route.
citation: BSL-2: Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane. BSL-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Scenario: A researcher handles Ebola virus. Specify the BSL and required personal containment.
back: BSL-4; requires positive-pressure air-fed suits or working within a Class III glove-box Biosafety Cabinet.
citation: BSL-4: Ebola virus... Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: What is the safety protocol for aerosol-generating procedures (e.g., vortexing) in BSL-2?
back: Must be performed within a Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) to prevent personnel exposure.
citation: BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Define Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) according to WHO.
back: Designations for lab facilities based on design, construction, equipment, and practices required to handle specific Risk Group agents.
citation: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Which BSL is required for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and what specific entry feature is mandatory?
back: BSL-3; requires a double-door entry airlock and continuous airflow monitoring.
citation: BSL-3: Mycobacterium tuberculosis... double-door entry airlock; BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Case: A lab lacks HEPA filtration and negative pressure. Can it safely process Bacillus anthracis?
back: No. B. anthracis (RG-3) requires BSL-3 facilities featuring negative air pressure and HEPA-filtered exhaust to prevent aerosol spread.
citation: BSL-3: Bacillus anthracis... Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Describe the mandatory wait time after a biological aerosol spill.
back: Evacuate immediately and wait 30 minutes before re-entering to allow aerosols to settle.
citation: If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: List two BSL-1 (Risk Group 1) organisms and their primary safety protocol.
back:
Organisms: E. coli (K-12), Bacillus subtilis.
Protocol: Open benchwork and standard microbiological practices.
citation: BSL-1: E. coli (K-12 strains), Bacillus subtilis... Standard microbiological practices; open benchwork.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Define Biosafety Levels (BSL) according to WHO.
back: Designations (1-4) assigned to labs based on design, construction, containment, and practices required to safely handle agents from various risk groups.

category: Describe biosafety levels

back: Controlled negative air pressure with directional airflow into the lab and HEPA filtration of all exhaust air.
citation: BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Contrast the primary transmission routes targeted by BSL-2 versus BSL-3 protocols.
back: BSL-2: Ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane hazards. BSL-3: Serious/lethal disease via inhalation or aerosol route.

citation: BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Identify two microbial examples and the bench requirement for BSL-1.
back: Agents: E. coli (K-12), B. subtilis. Bench: Open benchwork with standard microbiological practices.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: When must a Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) be used in a BSL-2 laboratory?

citation: BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: A lab handles Mycobacterium tuberculosis. What specific facility entry and air monitoring are required?
back: Double-door entry airlock and continuous airflow monitoring (to ensure negative pressure).
citation: BSL-3: Mycobacterium tuberculosis... double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink; BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Describe the structural relationship between BSL-4 facilities and the main building.
back: Must be an isolated building or a strictly controlled, isolated zone within a building.
citation: BSL-4: Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits... full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: What is the maximum storage duration for biological waste in a dedicated room?
back: Maximum of 24 to 48 hours in a locked, ventilated, and marked room.
citation: Biological waste must be stored in a dedicated, locked, ventilated room marked with a biohazard symbol for a maximum of 24 to 48 hours.

back: A double-door entry airlock and continuous airflow monitoring.
citation: Section 1: BSL-3: double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink; BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Give two examples of 'Well-characterized agents' managed in BSL-1.
back: 1. E. coli K-12 strains. 2. Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast).
citation: Section 1: RG-1: Well-characterized agents... E. coli (K-12 strains), Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: How does the WHO define biosafety in laboratory containment?
back: Principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents or toxins and their accidental release.
citation: Source: Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Which specific factors determine the assigned Biosafety Level (BSL) of a laboratory facility?
back: Combination of laboratory design, construction, containment equipment, practices, and operational procedures required for specific risk groups.
citation: Source: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures...

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Differentiate BSL-1 and BSL-2 based on the nature of organisms handled.
back: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to cause disease (e.g., E. coli K-12). BSL-2: Moderate hazards (e.g., HIV, Hepatitis B/C).
citation: Source: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease... BSL-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards to personnel and the environment.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: What laboratory level and specific PPE are mandatory for handling Ebola or CCHF viruses?
back: BSL-4. Requires an isolated building/zone, positive-pressure air-fed suits, and a full chemical decontamination shower upon exit.
citation: Source: BSL-4: Ebola virus... Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus. Safety Protocols: Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits... full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Describe the specific air containment requirements for a BSL-3 laboratory.
back: Controlled negative air pressure with directional airflow into the lab and mandatory HEPA filtration of all exhaust air.
citation: Source: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Define Risk Group 3 (RG-3) agents handled in BSL-3 facilities.
back: Indigenous or exotic agents that cause serious or lethal disease specifically through the inhalation or aerosol route.
citation: Source: RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: When is the use of a Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) mandatory in a BSL-2 laboratory?
back: During aerosol-generating procedures, including centrifugation and vortexing, to prevent inhalation exposure of moderate-hazard personnel agents.
citation: Source: BSL-2: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC Class I or II) used for aerosol-generating procedures (centrifugation, vortexing).

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: A facility handles Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Which BSL is required and what entry protocol is essential?
back: BSL-3. Essential protocols include a double-door entry airlock and continuous monitoring of directional airflow.
citation: Source: BSL-3 Bio-Risk Organisms: Mycobacterium tuberculosis... Safety Protocols: double-door entry airlock; BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: Contrast the air filtration systems of BSL-3 versus BSL-4 facilities.
back: BSL-3 uses HEPA-filtered exhaust. BSL-4 requires a dedicated air supply and a double-HEPA filtered exhaust system.
citation: Source: BSL-3: HEPA filtration of exhaust air. BSL-4: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Define biosafety and biosafety levels according to WHO
front: Q: List four common pathogens typically managed under BSL-2 containment.
back: 1. Staphylococcus aureus. 2. Salmonella species. 3. Hepatitis B/C viruses. 4. Vibrio cholerae.
citation: Source: BSL-2 Bio-Risk Organisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella spp., Hepatitis B & C viruses, HIV, Vibrio cholerae.

category: Describe biosafety levels
coreConcept: WHO Biosafety Level Classification and Containment Protocols
front: What are the four Biosafety Levels (BSL) and their defining facility containment features?
back:
- BSL-1: Low-risk agents; standard open benchwork.
- BSL-2: Moderate hazards (e.g., HIV); Biosafety Cabinets (BSC); restricted access.
- BSL-3: Lethal aerosol agents (e.g., TB); negative air pressure; HEPA filtration.
- BSL-4: Life-threatening exotic agents (e.g., Ebola); positive-pressure suits; isolated building.
citation: Section 1: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures... [BSL-3 features] Controlled negative air pressure... HEPA filtration of exhaust air... [BSL-4 features] positive-pressure air-fed suits.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: How does the WHO define Biosafety in laboratory settings?
back: The containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents or their accidental release.
citation: 1. Biosafety & Biosafety Levels: Biosafety refers to the containment principles, technologies, and practices implemented to prevent unintentional exposure to biological agents and toxins, or their accidental release.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: What is the primary physiological/facility mechanism for aerosol containment in BSL-3 labs?
back:
- Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab).
- HEPA filtration of exhaust air.
- Double-door entry airlock.
citation: BSL-3 Safety Protocols: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Contrast BSL-2 and BSL-3 facilities regarding pathogen transmission and access.
back:
- BSL-2: Moderate hazards (Ingestion/Mucous membrane); restricted access.
- BSL-3: Lethal indigenous/exotic agents (Inhalation/Aerosol); double-door airlock and negative pressure.
citation: BSL-2: Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane... Restricted lab access. BSL-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: A lab worker handles Ebola or CCHF virus. Identify the required BSL level and PPE.
back:
- Level: BSL-4.
- PPE/Facility: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; isolated building zone.
citation: BSL-4 Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus... Safety Protocols: Positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: What is the mandatory chronological step for aerosol management after a laboratory spill?
back:
1. Evacuate room immediately.
2. Wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle.
3. Re-enter only after donning full PPE.
citation: Steps for the Management of a Laboratory Spill: 1. Evacuate & Alert... If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

back:
1. Primary Receptacle: Leak-proof tube with absorbent.

3. Outer Packaging: Rigid box with UN 3373 Diamond Label.
citation: 5. Transportation of Biological Samples: Triple Packaging System (UN 3373)... [ Primary Receptacle ] ---> [ Secondary Packaging ] ---> [ Outer Rigid Box ]

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Differentiate the disposal methods for human placentas versus used surgical scalpels.
back:
- Placentas: Yellow Bag; High-temp incineration (>1100°C).
- Scalpels: White puncture-proof container; Autoclaving/Dry heat followed by encapsulation.
citation: Infectious & Anatomical Waste: Human tissues, organs... Yellow Bag... High-Temperature Incineration. Sharps Waste: Needles, scalpels... White Container... Autoclaving / Dry Heat followed by encapsulation.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Explain the disinfection loop for cleaning a biological spill (Disinfectant and time).
back:
1. Cover with absorbent towels.
2. Apply 10% Sodium Hypochlorite (freshly prepared).
3. Observe contact time of 20-30 minutes.
citation: Spill Management: Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite... Observe Contact Time: Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes.

citation: BSL-1: Well-characterized agents not known to consistently cause disease in immunocompetent adult humans... Safety Protocols: Standard microbiological practices; open benchwork; handwashing sink.

category: Describe biosafety levels

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Define Biosafety Levels (BSL) according to WHO guidelines.
back: Designations (BSL 1-4) assigned to laboratory facilities based on design, containment, equipment, and procedures required to handle specific biological risk groups safely.
citation: Biosafety Levels (BSL 1 to 4) are designations assigned to biological laboratory facilities based on a combination of laboratory design, construction, containment facilities, equipment, practices, and operational procedures required to work with agents from various risk groups.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Contrast the transmission routes of Risk Group 2 versus Risk Group 3 agents.
back:
● BSL-2 (RG-2): Ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane contact.
● BSL-3 (RG-3): Serious or lethal disease transmission via inhalation/aerosol route.
citation: BSL-2: RG-2: Agents that pose moderate hazards... Transmission via ingestion, percutaneous, or mucous membrane. BSL-3: RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: What are the specific facility airflow requirements for a BSL-3 laboratory?
back:
● Controlled negative air pressure.
● Directional airflow into the lab.
● HEPA filtration of exhaust air.
citation: BSL-3 Facility Features: Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: A lab must isolate Ebola virus. Which BSL is required and what is the mandatory exit protocol?
back:
● Level: BSL-4.
● Protocol: Exit through a full chemical decontamination shower while wearing a positive-pressure air-fed suit.
citation: BSL-4: Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus... Safety Protocols: positive-pressure air-fed suits... full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: What is the required disinfectant concentration and contact time for biological spill management?
back:
● Disinfectant: 10% Sodium Hypochlorite (freshly prepared).
● Contact Time: 20 to 30 minutes undisturbed.
citation: Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite / household bleach solution)... Observe Contact Time: Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes for microbial inactivation.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: List three common bio-risk organisms classified under BSL-2.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Why is a 30-minute waiting period mandatory after an aerosol-generating spill?
back: To allow potentially infectious aerosols to settle before re-entering the room with appropriate PPE (N95 respirator).
citation: If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Differentiate the primary containment equipment used for BSL-3 vs BSL-4 labs.
back:
● BSL-3: Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) Class II or III.
● BSL-4: Class III glove-box BSC or positive-pressure suits in an isolated zone.
citation: BSL-3: BSC Class II or III. BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: Outline the Triple Packaging System (UN 3373) layers for sample transport.
back:
1. Primary Receptacle: Leak-proof + absorbent wrap.
2. Secondary Packaging: Leak-proof and durable.
3. Outer Packaging: Rigid box with UN 3373 diamond label.
citation: [ Primary Receptacle ] (Leak-proof + Absorbent) ---> [ Secondary Packaging ] (Leak-proof & Durable) ---> [ Outer Rigid Box ] (UN 3373 + Markings)

category: Describe biosafety levels
front: Q: What is the maximum storage time for biological waste in a dedicated room?
back: Maximum of 24 to 48 hours in a locked, ventilated room with a biohazard symbol.
citation: Storage Rules: Biological waste must be stored in a dedicated, locked, ventilated room marked with a biohazard symbol for a maximum of 24 to 48 hours.

front: Q: What is the sink requirement for personnel hygiene in BSL-3 labs?
back: The laboratory must be equipped with a hands-free sink.
citation: Table 1: [BSL-3] hands-free sink.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: How does BSL-3 respiratory protection differ from BSL-2 during aerosol-generating procedures?
back: BSL-3 strictly requires Airborne Precautions, including fitted N95 or FFP2 respirators.
citation: Section 4 PPE: [Airborne Precautions] Fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator... (Mycobacterium tuberculosis).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What safety feature ensures the ventilation system in BSL-3 is functioning correctly?
back: The facility must maintain continuous airflow monitoring.
citation: Table 1: [BSL-3] continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: In the event of an aerosol-generating spill in BSL-3, how long is evacuation mandatory?
back: Personnel must evacuate immediately and wait at least 30 minutes for aerosols to settle.
citation: Section 3: [Spill Management] If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Which Risk Group (RG) and transmission route characterize Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3)?
back:
• Risk Group 3 (RG-3).
• Transmission: Inhalation or aerosol route causing serious/lethal disease.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3] RG-3: Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Explain the 'directional airflow' requirement for a BSL-3 laboratory facility.
back:
• Controlled negative air pressure.
• Airflow moves strictly from clean areas into the contaminated lab.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Contrast the exhaust air treatment of BSL-3 versus BSL-2 facilities.
back:
• BSL-3: Mandatory HEPA filtration of all exhaust air.
• BSL-2: HEPA filtration not strictly required for general exhaust.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3] HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: A lab processes Mycobacterium tuberculosis. What specific facility design prevents environmental aerosol release?
back:
• Controlled negative air pressure.
• HEPA-filtered exhaust air.
• Double-door airlock entry.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3] Mycobacterium tuberculosis... Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Which specific Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) classes are required for BSL-3 procedures?
back:
• BSC Class II.
• BSC Class III.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 Safety Protocols] BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Name three high-yield bacterial and viral pathogens requiring BSL-3 containment.
back:
• Bacteria: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Bacillus anthracis.
• Virus: SARS-CoV-2.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 Bio-Risk Organisms] Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Brucella spp., Bacillus anthracis, SARS-CoV-2.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Describe the structural entry requirement for a BSL-3 laboratory to maintain containment.
back:
• Double-door entry.
• Must utilize an airlock system.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 Safety Protocols] double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink; BSC Class II or III.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: Why is BSL-3 insufficient for handling Ebola virus instead of BSL-4?
back:
• Ebola is RG-4 (Life-threatening/no vaccine).
• BSL-3 lacks positive-pressure suits and dedicated double-HEPA exhaust.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4] Ebola virus... Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What feature must be present in BSL-3 to ensure the ventilation system is functioning?
back:
• Continuous airflow monitoring system.
• Visual/audible alarms for pressure loss.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 Safety Protocols] BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Q: What hand-hygiene facility is a mandatory design feature of a BSL-3 lab?
back:
• Hands-free sink.
• Usually located near the exit door.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3 Safety Protocols] double-door entry airlock; hands-free sink.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: List four high-risk viral agents handled in BSL-4 laboratories.
back:
1. Ebola virus
2. Marburg virus
3. Lassa virus
4. Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.
citation: Section 1: [Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Why are BSL-4 agents classified as Risk Group 4 (RG-4)?
back: They are dangerous/exotic agents causing life-threatening, aerosol-transmitted infections with no available vaccines or treatments.
citation: Section 1: [RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the primary containment equipment of BSL-4 with BSL-3.
back: BSL-4 uses positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSCs; BSL-3 uses Class II/III BSCs with negative air pressure.
citation: Section 1: [BSL-3: BSC Class II or III; BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What mandatory exit protocol must be followed when leaving a BSL-4 zone?
back: Personnel must undergo a full chemical decontamination shower.
citation: Section 1: [full chemical decontamination shower exit.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the exhaust air filtration requirement for a BSL-4 facility.
back: Exhaust air must undergo double-HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration.
citation: Section 1: [dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What are the two physical location requirements for a BSL-4 laboratory?
back:
1. Isolated building OR
2. Controlled isolated zone within a building.
citation: Section 1: [Isolated building/zone;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: How is the air supply managed in a BSL-4 suit laboratory?
back: The facility provides a dedicated air supply and maintains positive pressure within the protective suits.
citation: Section 1: [positive-pressure air-fed suits... dedicated air supply]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: In BSL-4, which specific BSC class is used in a 'Cabinet Laboratory' configuration?
back: Class III Biosafety Cabinet (Glove-box).
citation: Section 1: [Class III glove-box BSC;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What defines the community risk level for BSL-4 agents?
back: High community risk due to potential for rapid aerosol transmission and high mortality.
citation: Section 1: [Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the primary difference between BSL-3 and BSL-4 regarding immunization?
back: BSL-3 agents may have vaccines (e.g., Anthrax); BSL-4 agents typically have no vaccines or treatments.
citation: Section 1: [BSL-4: life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which specific viral agents are handled within a BSL-4 laboratory setting?
back:
- Ebola virus
- Marburg virus
- Lassa virus
- Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus
citation: Section 1: [Bio-Risk Organisms BSL-4] Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What unique personal protective equipment (PPE) is mandatory for personnel in BSL-4?
back:
- One-piece positive-pressure air-fed suits
- Dedicated air supply for the suit
- Chemical decontamination shower upon exit
citation: Section 1: [Safety Protocols BSL-4] positive-pressure air-fed suits... full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the exhaust air filtration systems of BSL-3 and BSL-4 laboratories.
back:
- BSL-3: Single HEPA filtration of exhaust air
- BSL-4: Dedicated double-HEPA filtration of exhaust air
citation: Section 1: [BSL-3 vs BSL-4] BSL-3: HEPA filtration of exhaust air; BSL-4: double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: A researcher is accidentally exposed to Ebola via suit breach. What BSL-4 protocol defines this agent?
back:
- Risk Group 4 (RG-4)
- High individual/community risk
- Aerosol-transmitted and life-threatening
- No available vaccines or treatments
citation: Section 1: [Risk Group 4] Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the primary pharmacological limitation defining a BSL-4 (RG-4) agent?
back:
- Absence of effective vaccines
- Absence of established therapeutic treatments for the specific infection
citation: Section 1: [BSL-4 Description] dangerous and exotic agents... with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the facility construction requirement for a BSL-4 laboratory.
back:
- Located in a separate, isolated building OR
- A clearly demarcated and isolated zone within a secure building
citation: Section 1: [Facility Features BSL-4] Isolated building/zone.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) type is used if a positive-pressure suit is NOT worn?
back:
- Class III Biosafety Cabinet (Glove-box BSC)
- Provides physical barrier between agent and researcher
citation: Section 1: [BSL-4 Protocols] positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Identify the mandatory exit procedure for all personnel leaving a BSL-4 suit room.
back:
- Must pass through a chemical decontamination shower
- Designed to neutralize surface bio-contaminants on the suit
citation: Section 1: [BSL-4] full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the airflow directionality required for BSL-4 containment maintenance.
back:
- Directed inward (negative pressure)
- Ensures that air always flows from clean areas to contaminated areas
citation: Section 1: [General High Containment] Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab).

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the mandatory labeling for the outer packaging of BSL-4 biological samples?
back:
- UN 3373 Diamond Label
- Biohazard symbol
- Sender/Recipient contact details
- 24/7 Emergency contact info
citation: Section 5: [Outer Packaging] rigid outer box bearing the UN 3373 Diamond Label, Biohazard symbol... and 24/7 emergency contact details.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What are the core characteristics of Risk Group 3 agents handled in BSL-3?
back:
1. Indigenous or exotic agents.
2. Cause serious or lethal disease.
3. Transmitted primarily via inhalation or aerosols.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [Indigenous or exotic agents that may cause serious or potentially lethal disease through inhalation/aerosol route.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: How does controlled negative air pressure maintain safety in a BSL-3 laboratory?
back:
1. Creates directional airflow into the lab.
2. Prevents contaminated aerosols from escaping to adjacent non-contained areas.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [Controlled negative air pressure (directional airflow into lab); HEPA filtration of exhaust air.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Contrast the facility entry requirements between BSL-2 and BSL-3 laboratories.
back:
1. BSL-2: Restricted access and biohazard signs.
2. BSL-3: Mandatory double-door entry airlock and continuous airflow monitoring.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [BSL-2: Restricted lab access; biohazard warning signs... BSL-3: double-door entry airlock; continuous airflow monitoring.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: A BSL-3 technician suspects a Mycobacterium tuberculosis aerosol release. What is the immediate protocol?
back:
1. Evacuate and alert personnel immediately.
2. Wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.
3. Re-enter wearing N95 respirator and full PPE.
citation: Section 3: [If an aerosol is generated, evacuate the room immediately and wait 30 minutes for aerosols to settle before re-entering.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Specify the disinfectant concentration and contact time required for decontaminating BSL-3 spills.
back:
1. Disinfectant: 10% Sodium Hypochlorite (freshly prepared).
2. Contact Time: 20 to 30 minutes for microbial inactivation.
citation: Section 3: [Apply Disinfectant: Pour a freshly prepared disinfectant (10% Sodium Hypochlorite... Allow an undisturbed contact time of 20 to 30 minutes.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: List four high-yield bio-risk organisms that mandate BSL-3 containment protocols.
back:
1. Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
2. Brucella spp.
3. Bacillus anthracis.
4. SARS-CoV-2.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Brucella spp., Bacillus anthracis, SARS-CoV-2.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What is the mandatory requirement for exhaust air treatment in a BSL-3 facility?
back: All exhaust air must undergo HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration before being discharged outside the facility.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [HEPA filtration of exhaust air; double-door entry airlock.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Why is Ebola virus handled in BSL-4 instead of BSL-3 despite being aerosol-transmitted?
back: BSL-3 is for agents with possible treatments/vaccines. Ebola (BSL-4) is life-threatening with no widely available vaccines or treatments and high community risk.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [BSL-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk... with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: Explain the role of the Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) in the BSL-3 airflow loop.
back:
1. BSC Class II or III is mandatory for all procedures.
2. It provides primary containment for aerosols at the source before they reach the room environment.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring... used for aerosol-generating procedures.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 3
front: What specific hand-hygiene facility feature is required at the exit of a BSL-3 lab?
back: A hands-free sink (foot-pedal or sensor-operated) must be available near the exit to prevent cross-contamination.
citation: Section 1, Table 1: [hands-free sink; BSC Class II or III; continuous airflow monitoring.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: List four high-risk viral pathogens that require BSL-4 containment according to WHO guidelines.
back:
- Ebola virus
- Marburg virus
- Lassa virus
- Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the mandatory personal protective attire used when working in a BSL-4 'suit' laboratory.
back: Personnel must wear positive-pressure air-fed suits connected to a dedicated, external breathing air supply.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; dedicated air supply]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the BSC requirements of BSL-4 with BSL-3 facilities.
back:
- BSL-3: Class II or III BSC
- BSL-4: Specifically Class III glove-box BSC (or air-fed suits)
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3: BSC Class II or III; BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: A researcher is handling Marburg virus. What is the mandatory exit procedure from the containment zone?
back: Personnel must perform a full chemical decontamination shower exit before leaving the BSL-4 facility.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [full chemical decontamination shower exit.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Specify the exhaust air filtration requirement for a BSL-4 facility.
back: Exhaust air must be filtered through a dedicated double-HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration system.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Define the Risk Group (RG) characteristics that mandate BSL-4 containment.
back: RG-4: Dangerous/exotic agents with high individual/community risk, aerosol transmission, and no available vaccines or treatments.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the structural location requirement for a BSL-4 laboratory.
back: The lab must be in a completely isolated building or a strictly segregated zone with controlled access.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Isolated building/zone]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: How is the atmosphere within a BSL-4 Class III BSC (glove box) isolated from the operator?
back: The cabinet is gas-tight and sealed; materials are manipulated via heavy-duty rubber gloves attached to the cabinet.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Class III glove-box BSC]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the primary difference in air supply between BSL-3 and BSL-4 labs?
back: BSL-3 uses negative directional airflow; BSL-4 requires a dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-3: Controlled negative air pressure; BSL-4: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Name the specific hemorrhagic fever virus common in Pakistan that requires BSL-4 containment.
back: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Identify the specific Risk Group (RG) and transmission route associated with BSL-4 facilities.
back: Risk Group 4 (RG-4). These involve dangerous, exotic agents posing high risk for aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Why are BSL-4 pathogens like Ebola considered high-risk regarding medical intervention?
back: They cause life-threatening infections for which no effective vaccines or specific treatments are currently available.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4... life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Contrast the respiratory PPE requirements for BSL-4 versus BSL-3 laboratories.
back: BSL-3 uses N95 respirators. BSL-4 requires positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III (glove-box) Biosafety Cabinets.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; BSL-3: N95 respirator].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: A researcher handling CCHF virus leaves the laboratory. Name the mandatory terminal exit procedure.
back: A full chemical decontamination shower is mandatory before exiting the BSL-4 containment zone.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: full chemical decontamination shower exit].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Which specific air filtration engineering control ensures exhaust air from a BSL-4 lab is sterile?
back: The facility must utilize double-HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration for all exhaust air.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: List four high-yield viral examples handled exclusively in BSL-4 laboratories.
back:
1. Ebola virus
2. Marburg virus
3. Lassa virus
4. Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4 Bio-Risk Organisms: Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Describe the architectural location requirements for a BSL-4 facility compared to standard labs.
back: BSL-4 labs must be located in an isolated building or a strictly controlled, isolated zone.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: Isolated building/zone].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Differentiate between the two primary containment configurations used for BSL-4 laboratory benchwork.
back:
1. Suit Lab: Personnel wear positive-pressure suits.
2. Cabinet Lab: Work is done in Class III glove-box BSCs.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: How does a positive-pressure air-fed suit maintain protection if the suit material is punctured?
back: Higher internal air pressure prevents contaminated laboratory air from entering the suit via the breach.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: What is the primary route of transmission that BSL-4 facility protocols are designed to eliminate?
back: Transmission via infectious aerosols (airborne/inhalation route) causing life-threatening community and individual risks.
citation: Page 1 (Book Page): [BSL-4: posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted... infections].

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which Risk Group (RG) of biological agents is managed within BSL-4 facilities?
back: Risk Group 4 (RG-4): Dangerous and exotic agents causing life-threatening, aerosol-transmitted infections with no available vaccines or treatments.
citation: Source: [BSL-4] RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: How do positive-pressure suits protect personnel working in a BSL-4 laboratory environment?
back: They provide a dedicated air supply and maintain higher internal pressure to prevent contaminated lab air from entering the suit.
citation: Source: [BSL-4] positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC; dedicated air supply.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the air exhaust filtration requirements between BSL-3 and BSL-4 facilities.
back: BSL-3 requires HEPA filtration of exhaust air; BSL-4 requires mandatory double-HEPA filtration for exhaust.
citation: Source: [BSL-3] HEPA filtration of exhaust air. [BSL-4] double-HEPA exhaust.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: A researcher is exiting a BSL-4 suit area. Which mandatory decontamination step must be completed?
back: A full chemical decontamination shower is required upon exiting the BSL-4 laboratory zone.
citation: Source: [BSL-4] full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the mandatory chemical intervention used for personnel decontamination in BSL-4 exits?
back: A chemical decontamination shower designed to neutralize biological agents on the exterior of personal protective equipment.
citation: Source: [BSL-4 Safety Protocols] full chemical decontamination shower exit.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What are the defining criteria for a pathogen to be classified as Bio-Risk Group 4?
back: 1. High individual/community risk. 2. Aerosol transmission. 3. Life-threatening disease. 4. No effective vaccine or treatment.
citation: Source: [BSL-4 Description] Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: If a BSL-4 lab lacks air-fed suits, which specific primary containment equipment must be used?
back: Class III Biosafety Cabinet (Glove-box), which provides a physical barrier between the agent and the worker.
citation: Source: [BSL-4] positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: A facility is being designed to handle Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF). Which BSL level is mandatory?
back: BSL-4, as CCHF is a dangerous, life-threatening virus with high community risk.
citation: Source: [BSL-4 Bio-Risk Organisms] Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Describe the directional airflow loop required for BSL-4 laboratory safety.
back: Controlled negative air pressure ensures air flows from clean areas into the lab, followed by double-HEPA filtration before exhaust.
citation: Source: [BSL-4] Dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust; [BSL-3 context] Controlled negative air pressure.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: List three high-risk viral agents that require BSL-4 containment according to WHO guidelines.
back: 1. Ebola virus. 2. Marburg virus. 3. Lassa virus.
citation: Source: [BSL-4 Bio-Risk Organisms] Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus.

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: How many HEPA filters are mandatory for the exhaust air system in a BSL-4 laboratory?
back: Double-HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filtration.
citation: BSL-4: ...dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust;

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Which specific Risk Group (RG) characteristics necessitate BSL-4 containment for pathogens like Ebola?
back: Dangerous, exotic agents posing high individual/community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections lacking available vaccines or treatments.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [RG-4: Dangerous and exotic agents posing high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Explain the unique air filtration requirement for BSL-4 exhaust systems.
back: BSL-4 facilities must utilize a dedicated air supply and a double-HEPA exhaust system to ensure absolute containment of aerosols.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Safety Protocols & Facility Features: dedicated air supply and double-HEPA exhaust;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Contrast the primary containment equipment used in BSL-4 versus BSL-3 labs.
back: BSL-4 uses positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSCs; BSL-3 typically uses Class II or III BSCs.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-4: positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC... BSL-3: BSC Class II or III;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: A researcher is handling Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus. What specific suit and exit protocols apply?
back:
1. Positive-pressure air-fed suit
2. Mandatory full chemical decontamination shower exit
3. Facility isolated in a separate building/zone.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Bio-Risk Organisms: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) virus... Safety Protocols: positive-pressure air-fed suits... full chemical decontamination shower exit.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: What is the mandatory step for personnel before exiting a BSL-4 'suit' laboratory?
back: Personnel must undergo a full chemical decontamination shower to neutralize any potential pathogens on the exterior of the pressure suit.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [Safety Protocols & Facility Features: full chemical decontamination shower exit.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: List the two primary facility design configurations allowed for BSL-4 laboratories.
back:
1. Cabinet Laboratory: Work done in Class III BSC (glove-box).
2. Suit Laboratory: Personnel wear positive-pressure suits in an isolated zone.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-4: Isolated building/zone; positive-pressure air-fed suits or Class III glove-box BSC;]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4
front: Q: Why is BSL-4 containment designated as an 'Isolated Zone' within a building?
back: To ensure maximum separation from the public and other lab areas, preventing community transmission of lethal, untreatable agents.
citation: Patient safety ID.md: [BSL-4: Isolated building/zone... high individual and community risk of aerosol-transmitted, life-threatening infections with no vaccines/treatments.]

category: Discuss the safety protocols of BSL 4

front: Q: What is the formal definition of Biological Waste?
back: Waste generated during diagnosis, research, or treatment containing viable microorganisms, tissues, blood, or fluids capable of causing infection.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Biological Waste: Any waste generated during biological diagnosis, research, immunization, or treatment containing viable microorganisms, cultured material, human tissues, blood, or body fluids capable of causing infection.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Why is human tissue categorized specifically as Infectious and Anatomical waste?
back: These materials harbor viable pathogens or cellular components capable of transmitting disease to personnel or the environment if not incinerated.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Infectious & Anatomical Waste: Human tissues, organs... containing viable microorganisms... capable of causing infection.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Contrast the disposal protocols for yellow bags versus red bags.
back: • Yellow: Infectious/Anatomical; High-temp incineration (>1100°C). • Red: Recyclable plastics; Autoclaving/Microwaving followed by shredding.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Yellow Bag: Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C) or deep burial. Red Bag: Treated by Autoclaving or Microwaving followed by shredding.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: A surgeon finishes a procedure with a bloody scalpel. Describe the immediate disposal steps.
back: Place into a White, puncture-proof container without recapping; treat via Autoclaving or Dry Heat before final encapsulation.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Sharps Waste: Needles, scalpels... White Container (Translucent, Puncture-proof). Treated by Autoclaving / Dry Heat followed by encapsulation.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What are the specific thermal treatment requirements for Infectious and Anatomical waste?
back: High-temperature incineration reaching levels above 1100°C to ensure complete destruction of biological pathogens.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Yellow Bag... Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C).]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: What is the mandatory maximum duration for storing biological waste on-site?
back: Biological waste must be stored in a dedicated, ventilated area for a maximum of 24 to 48 hours.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Biological waste must be stored in a dedicated, locked, ventilated room... for a maximum of 24 to 48 hours.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: How must a facility manage the disposal of a human placenta after delivery?
back: Segregate into a Yellow Bag at the point of generation for incineration or deep burial.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Infectious & Anatomical Waste... placentas... Yellow Bag... Treated by High-Temperature Incineration (>1100°C) or deep burial.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Differentiate the disposal of IV bottles from contaminated glass ampoules.
back: • IV Bottles: Red Bag (Recyclable plastic). • Ampoules: Blue Box; disinfected with Sodium Hypochlorite/Autoclave, then recycled.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Red Bag: IV bottles... Blue Box / Bin: Contaminated glass bottles, ampoules... Disinfected with Sodium Hypochlorite / Autoclaving.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Describe the decontamination cycle for contaminated laboratory glassware.
back: 1. Segregate in Blue Bin. 2. Disinfect via Sodium Hypochlorite or Autoclaving. 3. Send for glass recycling.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [Glassware Waste: Blue Box / Bin... Disinfected with Sodium Hypochlorite / Autoclaving, then sent for glass recycling.]

category: Define biological waste
front: Q: Which bin color and disposal route are used for non-infectious food packaging?
back: Black or Green Bin; these items are sent directly to a municipal landfill.
citation: Page 2 (Book Page): [General Non-Infectious Waste: Office paper... food wrappers... Black / Green Bin... Sent directly to municipal landfill disposal.]

category: Categorize the biological wastes
front: Q: Categorize healthcare biological wastes by bin color and their specific disposal methods.
back:
1. Yellow: Infectious/Anatomical (Incineration >1100°C/Deep burial).
2. Red: Recyclable plastics (Autoclave/Microwave + Shredding).
3. White: Sharps (Autoclave/Dry Heat + Encapsulation).
4. Blue: Glassware (Sodium Hypochlorite/Autoclave + Recycling).
5. Black/Green: General waste (Landfill).
citation: Section 2 Biological Waste Management: Yellow Bag: Infectious & Anatomical Waste (Incineration); Red Bag: Contaminated Recyclable Plastics (Autoclave/Microwave/Shredding); White Container: Sharps Waste (Autoclave/Dry Heat/Encapsulation); Blue Box: Glassware Waste (Disinfection/Recycling); Black / Green Bin: General Non-Infectious Waste (Landfill).
